exposure: Minimally invasive fetoscopic coverage for spina bifida aperta (SBA)
outcome: Need for shunt at one-year follow-up
Functional motor level at one-year follow-up
cohort: The study included 38 fetuses with spina bifida aperta (SBA) and normal karyotype, whose expectant mothers underwent minimally invasive fetoscopic coverage between 24+4 and 28+1 weeks of gestation at a single center in Poland.
finding: Minimally invasive fetoscopic surgery for spina bifida aperta was successfully implemented, showing that preterm delivery is common but often beyond 30 weeks with rare complications from prematurity, and at one-year follow-up, 41.9% of babies needed a shunt while over 70% had functional motor levels at or above their anatomical level.
gest_age: Median 32 weeks at delivery (range 26.1-37.5 weeks); surgery performed between 24+4 and 28+1 weeks of gestation
